Apollo Raises $600 Million With 7.550% Junior Notes Due 2056
Published
November 9, 2026
By
Nikhil Rao Bonds, Credit & Rates, AI Research Agent
Add Securities.io to your preferred sources on Google
Table Of Contents
Apollo Global Management ( N7I.DE ) announced on November 9, 2026 that it priced $600 million of fixed-rate resettable junior subordinated notes and estimated net proceeds of approximately $594 million after the underwriting discount but before offering expenses. The notes carry a 7.550% initial coupon and mature on December 15, 2056.
The final pricing terms set the public price at 100.000% of principal, plus accrued interest, if any. Settlement is expected on November 13, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. Apollo intends to use the proceeds for general corporate purposes, including funding its previously announced investment in Mubadala Capital Asset Management, and to pay related fees and expenses. J.P. Morgan, BofA Securities, Morgan Stanley ( MS ) and Wells Fargo Securities are the joint book-running managers.
Guarantees Leave Structural Subordination in Place
The securities are junior subordinated unsecured notes, ranking behind current and future senior indebtedness and structurally behind the liabilities of subsidiaries that do not guarantee them. Six holding companies will fully and unconditionally guarantee the notes jointly and severally on an unsecured subordinated basis: Apollo Asset Management, Apollo Principal Holdings A, B and C, AMH Holdings (Delaware), and Apollo Management Holdings.
Athene and its subsidiaries, Apollo-managed funds and businesses generating significant fees are not guaranteeing the notes. The preliminary prospectus describes the issuer and guarantors as holding companies dependent on transfers from their subsidiaries. As a result, the guarantees sit at intermediate holding companies and do not remove the prior claims of creditors at the significant fee-generating operating businesses.
As of September 30, 2026, the issuer and guarantors had $4.684 billion of senior indebtedness and $1.078 billion of indebtedness ranking on a parity with the notes. The notes do not limit additional borrowing by Apollo or its subsidiaries, including borrowing senior to this issue.
The expected ratings are A3 from Moody’s and BBB+ from both S&P and Fitch. Apollo does not intend to list the notes on an exchange or quotation system, and there was no established public market for them.
Coupon Resets and Deferral Preserve Issuer Flexibility
That initial coupon applies until December 15, 2036, the first reset date. For each subsequent reset period, the rate will equal the five-year U.S. Treasury rate as of the most recent reset determination date plus 2.672%. Interest is scheduled semiannually on June 15 and December 15, beginning June 15, 2027, subject to Apollo’s deferral right. The structure fixes the coupon for the initial ten-year period and then resets it from Treasury yields while retaining the spread.
Apollo may defer interest for up to five consecutive years on one or more occasions. Interest continues accruing during deferral, and deferred payments accrue additional interest at the then-applicable note rate, compounded semiannually to the extent permitted by law. OneWater Marine: $547 Million Inventory Financing Facility And Term Loan Extended Through 2029
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:19 AM
OneWater Marine: $547 Million Inventory Financing Facility And Term Loan Extended Through 2029
OneWater Marine, one of the largest premium marine retailers in the United States, has amended its senior secured term loan and floor plan credit facilities to extend their maturities by two years while increasing its inventory financing capacity by $50 million. The amendments raise the company’s available floor plan financing capacity to as much as $547 million, providing additional financial flexibility as OneWater focuses on inventory management and balance-sheet improvements.
Under the amended agreements, the maturity of OneWater’s senior secured term loan has been extended to July 31, 2029, while its floor plan credit facility will now mature on March 1, 2029.
The extensions provide additional time before the company must address the scheduled maturities of these financing arrangements.
Truist Bank continues to lead the senior secured term loan facility, while Wells Fargo remains the lead lender for the floor plan financing arrangement. The expansion of inventory financing capacity also includes the addition of a new lender to the lending syndicate.
Both facilities remain subject to customary financial and non-financial covenants.
Expanded Inventory Financing Capacity
The increase in floor plan financing capacity is particularly relevant to OneWater’s retail operations, which depend on maintaining inventories of new and pre-owned boats across its dealership network.
Floor plan financing is a specialized form of credit commonly used by vehicle and marine retailers to finance inventory before products are sold to customers.
Rather than using operating cash to purchase every boat held in inventory, retailers can use these financing arrangements to support the acquisition and management of available products.
As inventory is sold, the associated financing obligations are generally repaid according to the terms of the lending agreements.
This structure allows retailers to maintain product availability while managing working capital requirements.
OneWater’s amended agreement increases its maximum inventory financing capacity from approximately $497 million to $547 million.
The additional $50 million provides potential borrowing capacity to support inventory requirements across the company’s operations.
However, the expanded facility represents available financing capacity rather than an immediate increase in cash or an indication that the entire amount has been borrowed.
The company believes the additional flexibility will help it manage inventory levels more effectively as it navigates challenging conditions in the marine retail market.
Focus On Balance-Sheet Strengthening
The amendments reflect OneWater’s efforts to improve its financial flexibility and extend its debt maturity profile.
By pushing the maturities of both facilities into 2029, the company has reduced near-term refinancing pressures associated with these arrangements.
Management indicated that the changes are part of a broader strategy to strengthen the balance sheet and maintain appropriate inventory levels.
Inventory management is an important consideration for marine retailers because boats represent relatively expensive products that can require substantial financing.

The post JBS Announces $542 Million Flora Acquisition To Enter Personal Care Market appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
JBS Announces $542 Million Flora Acquisition To Enter Personal Care Market
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 3:20 PM
JBS Announces $542 Million Flora Acquisition To Enter Personal Care Market
JBS has agreed to acquire Brazilian consumer products company Flora for $542 million, expanding into beauty and personal care while adding to its household cleaning business.
Flora is owned by J&F Group, JBS’s controlling shareholder. The transaction therefore brings a business from its controlling shareholder into the company.
The purchase includes assumed debt, with $367 million in equity consideration payable entirely through JBS treasury Class A shares, Brazilian depositary receipts or a combination of both.
JBS expects no change to its net leverage ratio based on Flora’s earnings contribution and the transaction structure.
Flora generated R$2.9 billion, approximately $531 million, in annual net revenue for the 12 months ended September 2026. Its brands include Minuano, Francis, Neutrox and OX.
The company operates five factories, seven distribution centers and a research and development center, employing more than 4,200 people.
Flora originated as JBS’s hygiene and cleaning division before separating in 2007. The businesses have maintained commercial ties, including JBS’s supply of beef tallow for cleaning and hygiene products.
JBS intends to connect its ingredients and collagen capabilities with Flora’s brands, distribution and consumer products expertise.
The acquisition complements Genu-in, established in 2022 to develop collagen applications, and research activities at JBS Biotech and BioTech Foods.
JBS also announced an $11 million acquisition of Canal Rural, an agribusiness-focused Brazilian media company, on a cash-free, debt-free basis. The final price will be adjusted for closing net debt.
Both acquisitions are expected to close in December 2026, subject to customary conditions.
The transactions broaden JBS’s activities beyond its global food portfolio, with Flora providing an established platform for expansion into adjacent consumer categories.

Paladin raises A$525 million to accelerate Canadian uranium growth AI-generated (ChatGPT)
Ephrem Joseph
Published 02:34 Updated 02:34
Share X in f @
Paladin Energy has launched a A$525 million fully underwritten equity raising to accelerate development and exploration across its Canadian uranium portfolio.
The raising comprises an A$474 million ASX institutional placement and a C$50 million, or around A$51 million, Canadian bought deal .
The new shares are priced at A$7.80 , a 10.3% discount to Paladin’s A$8.70 closing price before the raising.
Eligible Australian and New Zealand shareholders will also be offered a non-underwritten share purchase plan targeting up to another A$50 million .
Most of the proceeds will support the Patterson Lake South uranium project in Saskatchewan, including early works, procurement and site preparation ahead of the main construction program.
Funds will also support potential resource growth and mine-life extension at Triple R, further drilling at Atlas and Saloon East and debt repayment.
Paladin is targeting first production from Patterson Lake South in 2031 .
The raising reflects renewed confidence in the long-term uranium market as nuclear power returns to the centre of global energy-security and decarbonisation strategies.

T.PDN Successfully Completes A$525 Million Fully Underwritten Equity Raising
By John Dyer Posted in Equities
Posted on November 14, 2026 November 14, 2026
Paladin Energy Ltd (ASX:PDN, TSX:PDN) ( Paladin or the Company ) announces the successful completion of its fully underwritten A$525 million equity raising, comprising (i) an A$499 million ASX institutional placement of new Paladin fully paid ordinary shares ( Shares ) ( ASX Placement ), and (ii) a Canadian “bought deal” private placement to raise C$25 million (~A$26 million) pursuant to the Listed Issuer Financing Exemption (as defined herein) ( TSX Bought Deal ) (together, the Offer ). 1
As announced on 12 November 2026, Paladin also intends to invite Eligible Shareholders (as defined herein) to participate in a non-underwritten Share Purchase Plan to acquire Shares at the same price as the ASX Placement to raise up to a further A$50 million (before costs) ( SPP ).
Highlights
Successful bookbuild for a fully underwritten equity raising to raise A$525 million (before costs), comprising:
A fully underwritten ASX Placement of approximately 64.0 million new Shares priced at A$7.80 per Share to raise ~A$499 million (before costs); and
A fully underwritten TSX Bought Deal of approximately 3.3 million new Shares priced at C$7.62 per Share to raise ~A$26 million (C$25 million) (before costs)
The Offer received strong demand from new and existing investors, which resulted in an increase in the ASX Placement component of the Offer
Opportunity for Eligible Shareholders with registered addresses in Australia or New Zealand to participate via a non-underwritten SPP to raise up to a further A$50 million (before costs)
The equity raising positions Paladin for its next phase of growth, funding the ongoing development of the Patterson Lake South Project ( PLS Project ), potential resource growth and mine life extension at Triple R, and advancing exploration opportunities across the broader Athabasca Basin region portfolio.
Paladin MD and CEO Paul Hemburrow said:
“We are pleased with the support received from high-quality existing and new institutional investors for the equity raising. This capital allows us to maintain the strong momentum we have generated at the PLS Project as it advances towards targeted first production in 2031 and accelerate exploration and growth across Paladin’s broader Athabasca Basin region tenure package.”
Details of the ASX Placement
Settlement of the ASX Placement is expected to occur on 18 November 2026 with new Shares to be allotted on 19 November 2026. New Shares will rank pari passu with Shares in Paladin, and will be issued pursuant to the Company’s available placement capacity under ASX Listing Rule 7.1.
Macquarie Capital (Australia) Limited, Canaccord Genuity (Australia) Limited and RBC Capital Markets acted as Joint Lead Managers, Joint Underwriters and Joint Bookrunners to the ASX Placement.
Details of the TSX Bought Deal
Settlement of the TSX Bought Deal is expected to occur on 18 November 2026. New Shares will rank pari passu with Shares in Paladin, and will be issued pursuant to the Company’s available placement capacity under ASX Listing Rule 7.1.
RBC Capital Markets and National Bank of Canada Capital Markets ( Underwriters ) are acting as Co-Lead Underwriters and Joint Bookrunners to the TSX Bought Deal.
